subject: GlideBio private offer: approval stacking, credits, and term options
messages:
From: Stephanie Flores <stephanie@glidebio.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: private offer structure for multi-division crediting and 12m term

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and finance teams want to run this via AWS Marketplace private offer to take advantage of resale and consolidated invoicing. A couple of specific asks from our side: 

- We have two business units (R&D and Clinical Ops). Can the private offer apply a single committed credit pool across both divisions, or do we need separate POs/offers?
- We prefer a 12-month term but want a 30% first-year consumption credit applied against usage rather than an upfront prepay. Is that structure supported?
- Which internal buyer approvals at AWS or within the buyer org typically block acceptance (e.g., legal signoff only, or procurement + security + finance)?

I've attached a short request summary and our procurement contact (cc'd). If it helps, can we do a short 30-min sync early next week to align on feasibility and timeline?

Best,
Stephanie Flores
Head of Procurement — GlideBio
stephanie@glidebio.com

Attachment: GlideBio_Marketplace_Request.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Flores <stephanie@glidebio.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: private offer structure for multi-division crediting and 12m term

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear summary and the PDF. Quick answers up front and then proposed next steps: 

- Single credit pool: Short answer — often yes, but it depends on the buyer's invoicing model and whether they want consolidated billing across divisions. AWS Marketplace supports consolidated billing under the same payer account; we have set up private offers that draw from a single purchase order/commit applied by the payer. If the two BUs are separate payer accounts, you'll need separate offers. 

- Consumption credit vs. prepay: We can structure a private offer that includes a usage credit (applied as a line-item discount against invoices), but implementation typically requires coordination with AWS Marketplace ops to map the credit to Redwood's offering SKU. A 30% first-year consumption credit is feasible as a contractual term; AWS will need to confirm how that's reflected on invoices (credit vs. reimbursement).

- Buyer approvals: In my experience the pipeline that causes delay is: procurement signoff (PO issuance) -> billing/payer alignment -> legal review (T&Cs/DPAs) -> security/compliance if there are data residency or integration considerations. AWS Marketplace sometimes requires the AWS account owner or marketplace admin to accept the private offer — that step can be quick but is a common gating item.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Quick sync (30 min) with your procurement + our AWS rep to validate payer account topology and invoicing flow.
2) We will draft the private offer terms and a short mutual action plan (MAP) that lists approval owners and estimated SLAs. 

Are you available Wed 19 May 9:00–10:00 PT or Thu 20 May 13:00–14:00 PT?

Thanks — I'll attach our standard PO template for your legal/procurement to review (see attached).

— Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_PO_Template_v2.docx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Inquiry: private offer structure for multi-division crediting and 12m term

Monica / Vivek —

Forwarding Stephanie's request and Monica's reply. A couple of operational notes from pricing/marketplace side: 

- If GlideBio wants a usage-credit model, we should scope whether the credit is an upfront "marketing credit" Redwood pays back to the buyer (we manually issue credits) or a line-item discount on the AWS invoice. The latter is cleaner for buyer accounting but requires AWS Marketplace Ops to accept the seller-side pricing adjustments. 

- Recommend we propose two parallel options in the MAP: (A) single-payer 12m private offer with line-item credit (preferred), (B) two linked private offers if they insist on separate payer accounts. Include an explicit acceptance path and who clicks accept in the buyer org. 

- Buyer approval stacking: identify the names/titles for procurement, legal, billing admin, and cloud ops. If any of those are a separate corporate shared-services org, add 2–3 business days to the forecast.

I can lead the MAP and coordinate with AWS rep once we have the sync scheduled. Vivek, can you confirm whether finance is comfortable with a 30% first-year consumption credit as an allowed discount for this segment?

— Vanessa
Director, Marketplace Sales Ops
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Flores <stephanie@glidebio.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: private offer structure for multi-division crediting and 12m term

Hi all —

Thanks, Monica and Vanessa. Quick confirmation from finance: we can support a 30% first-year consumption credit provided the MAP documents the redemption mechanics (how credit is applied monthly), and the deal meets our minimum ACV threshold (DEAL-8721 meets that). We prefer the line-item discount on AWS invoices for transparency; it reduces reconciliation overhead for both sides.

Operational asks for the sync: 
- Stephanie: please confirm the payer account ID(s) that GlideBio will use and the name/email of the person who will accept the private offer in AWS (usually a marketplace admin).
- Monica/Vanessa: I'll approve the credit on finance side once the MAP includes a 12-month term, credit schedule (months 1–12 with 30% applied to month 1–12 usage), and confirmation that there are no additional pass-through GST/VAT complications.

If we can get the payer topology and acceptance owner by Monday 24 May, we can aim to submit a private offer to AWS the week of 31 May.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
